reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Erythroplakia is more dangerous than leukoplakia histologically
Facial nerve palsy with parotid mass means malignancy until proven otherwise
Adenoid cystic carcinoma invades nerves and metastasises late to lungs
Persistent parotid enlargement in Sjogren syndrome needs MALT lymphoma exclusion
reference.pathophysiology: Chronic carcinogen bathing dysplasias oral mucosa in fields (leukoplakia to carcinoma sequence) while HPV E6 E7 disables tumour suppressors in oropharyngeal tonsil tissue. Salivary neoplasia arises from ductal reserve cells whose differentiation programmes (myoepithelial, mucus, serous) write the mixed histologies and invasion habits.
additionalDifferentials: Leukoplakia versus lichen planus versus candidiasis scrapability
Pleomorphic adenoma versus Warthin versus malignant salivary tumours
Adenoid cystic perineural versus mucoepidermoid patterns
additionalInvestigations: Biopsy of any oral patch or ulcer persisting beyond two to three weeks
Facial nerve assessment and imaging before parotid surgery
Fine needle aspiration cytology for salivary masses
